name: Slack
summary: You can create an app and enable public distribution in an afternoon, with no review. The catch for AI agents: since 29 May 2025, commercially distributed apps that are not in the Slack Marketplace get 1 request/minute (15 messages) on conversations.history and conversations.replies - and the Marketplace requires 10+ active workspaces and a review of up to ~10 weeks.
difficulty_reason: OAuth itself is self-serve, but reading message history at useful rates requires Marketplace approval, which has an install threshold and a multi-week review.

effort.hands_on: 45-90 min (app + distribution); 1-2 days to prepare a Marketplace submission
effort.production: Same day for unlisted distribution (throttled history reads); roughly 2-12 weeks for Marketplace approval
effort.waiting_on: Reaching 10 active workspaces, then Slack's preliminary review (up to 10 business days) and functional review (up to 10 weeks).

bottom_line: Create the app from a manifest, request only the scopes you actually use, and activate public distribution so design partners can install it today. If your agent reads channel history or threads, treat the Marketplace as a launch dependency: start recruiting the 10 active workspaces immediately, and design around the 1 req/min limit (cache, use the Events API to receive messages as they arrive) until you are listed.
app_type: Slack app with granular bot/user token scopes, created at api.slack.com/apps (optionally from a manifest), then 'Activate Public Distribution'.

scope_paths.name: Read channel history and threads (typical for agents)
scope_paths.review: Unlisted: works but limited to 1 req/min, 15 objects. Marketplace review removes the limit.

scope_paths.name: Workspace-wide search or admin
scope_paths.review: Not accepted in Marketplace per review guide
scope_paths.time_to_production: Unlikely to be approved for distributed apps

prerequisites.detail: Create a free workspace you own.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS redirect, events and interactivity URLs
prerequisites.detail: Public distribution requires SSL on OAuth redirect and request URLs.
Hard prerequisite to submit to the Marketplace.

prerequisites.item: Test account, dummy data and demo video
prerequisites.detail: Reviewers install the app themselves and need credentials for any third-party service you connect.

stages.name: Create and configure the app
stages.goal: Your dev workspace has the app installed with a bot token.

steps.title: Create app from manifest
steps.detail: An agent can generate the YAML manifest (scopes, redirect URLs, event subscriptions); you paste it at api.slack.com/apps > Create New App > From a manifest.

steps.title: Implement oauth.v2.access exchange
steps.detail: Authorise at https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize; store per-team bot token (and user token if requested). Bot tokens do not expire unless you enable token rotation.

stages.name: Distribute (unlisted)
stages.goal: Any workspace can install via your Add to Slack link.

steps.title: Complete the Manage Distribution checklist
steps.detail: Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces: fix each checklist item (HTTPS URLs etc.), then Activate Public Distribution.

steps.title: Design around Tier 1 history limits
steps.detail: Subscribe to message events and store what you need instead of polling conversations.history; queue history backfills at 1 req/min.

stages.name: Get listed in the Slack Marketplace
stages.goal: Full rate limits and a public listing.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Active = used in the past 28 days, on workspaces other than your dev workspace.

steps.title: Prepare submission
steps.detail: Agent drafts scope justifications (only for shipped features), listing copy, test-account instructions and the demo-video shot list. You record the video.

steps.title: Preliminary review
steps.detail: Listing, docs, scope justifications, installability. Resubmitting resets your queue position.

steps.title: Functional review
steps.detail: Reviewers test install, OAuth, setup, use and uninstall. Cannot be expedited for a launch date.

token_facts.value: Never expires unless token rotation is enabled (then 12h access token + single-use refresh token)

token_facts.fact: conversations.history / replies (unlisted, new installs since 29 May 2025)

gotchas.title: History rate limit for unlisted apps
gotchas.detail: Applies to new installs of unlisted apps since 29 May 2025. Existing installations are unaffected - so your own long-standing dev install will NOT reproduce what new customers experience.

gotchas.title: Marketplace won't approve scopes for unbuilt features
gotchas.detail: Only request scopes for functionality that exists today; add more later via resubmission (up to 6 weeks).

gotchas.title: Some scopes are not accepted at all
gotchas.detail: The review guide lists broad workspace data access, admin.*, search:read and triggers:* among scopes not allowed.

gotchas.title: Disabling distribution uninstalls everywhere
gotchas.detail: Turning off public distribution removes the app from all workspaces except the original.

gotchas.title: Token rotation is a one-way switch
gotchas.detail: Once enabled it can't be disabled, and every refresh returns a new single-use refresh token. Decide before launch and serialise refreshes per workspace.

blockers.symptom: ratelimited errors on conversations.history after onboarding a new customer
blockers.cause: Unlisted app Tier 1 limit (1 req/min) for new installs.
blockers.next_step: Back off using Retry-After, switch to Events API ingestion, and prioritise Marketplace submission.
Run a design-partner programme on unlisted distribution until you reach the threshold.

blockers.cause: Missing scope justification, no test credentials, or the reviewer couldn't install.
blockers.next_step: Fix all feedback in one pass - resubmitting resets the queue position.

agent_can: Generate the app manifest with minimum scopes
Write OAuth, token storage and Events API ingestion code
Build a rate-limit-aware history backfill queue
Draft Marketplace scope justifications, listing copy and demo-video script
Track your active-workspace count against the 10-workspace threshold
you_must: Create the app and complete distribution in the Slack UI
Record the demo video and own reviewer correspondence

claims.claim: Unlisted commercially distributed apps get Tier 1 (1 req/min, 15 objects) on conversations.history and conversations.replies for apps created / installed on or after 29 May 2025; existing installs unaffected.
Internal customer-built apps keep 50+ req/min and up to 1,000 objects.
Marketplace submission requires 10 or more active workspaces (active in past 28 days).
Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks for new apps (6 weeks for updates).
claims.note: Checked 2026-11-03. These are maximums stated by Slack, not observed durations.

claims.claim: Public distribution is activated via a checklist with no review step and requires SSL on redirect/request URLs.
The authorize endpoint returns an HTML page (HTTP 200) for an invalid client_id rather than an OAuth error redirect.
claims.note: Probed with client_id=000.000; error is rendered in-page, so automated checks must parse HTML.

claims.claim: Without token rotation access tokens never expire; with rotation they last 12 hours, refresh tokens are single-use, and rotation cannot be turned off once enabled.

open_questions: Real Marketplace review durations vary with volume; the figures above are Slack's stated maximums.
Whether the history limit applies identically to user tokens vs bot tokens was not tested.
